title: Proper direct image preserves ambient sums of classical complexes
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, and $f:X\to Y$ a proper scheme morphism. Assume $e\geq0$ bounds all fibre dimensions after every base change [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-pc-base-change] [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Work in ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves and their unbounded pro-étale derived categories, with total K-injective $Rf_*$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. For every small family $(K_s)_{s\in I}$ of complexes with classical cohomology, the canonical ambient coproduct comparison is invertible:
$$\bigoplus_{s\in I}Rf_*K_s\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*\bigl(\bigoplus_{s\in I}K_s\bigr).$$
Classical means [sk-def-pe-classical-definition], and the comparison is the map whose composite with the $s$-th coprojection is $Rf_*(\iota_s)$. The family may be empty; no common cohomological bound or cohomological-dimension assumption on a ground field is imposed.

source.place: Étale statements, direct sums from finite cohomological dimension; old split steps 11–12

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A_T=\operatorname{Mod}(A_T)$ for $T=X,Y$, on small site representatives in one common universe containing $I$. These categories, and the corresponding étale module categories, are Grothendieck abelian and have enough injectives. Properness makes $f$ finite type, hence quasi-compact, and separated, hence quasi-separated. Thus all qcqs comparison and coproduct inputs below apply even if $Y$ is not quasi-compact. Since $A$ is finite and discrete, the two finite-discrete coefficient lemmas identify the coefficient ring $A_T$ of the statement with the constant ring sheaf $\nu_T^*A_{T,\mathrm{\acute et}}$, so the classical and comparison statements for constant coefficients below apply to $\mathcal A_T$.

source.place: Étale statements and Transfer: categories and qcqs hypotheses

proof.text: Ambient coproducts in each of these unbounded derived categories are represented by termwise coproducts, with their specified coprojections. The sum functor on each abelian category is exact: finite sums are exact, and an arbitrary sum is the filtered colimit of its finite partial sums, so use exact filtered colimits from step 1. Applying the exact-functor cohomology identity to this sum functor gives $H^q(\bigoplus_s L_s)=\bigoplus_s H^q(L_s)$ naturally. Exactness also preserves the kernel and cokernel in the explicit good-truncation formulas, so $\tau_{\le b}$ and $\tau_{\ge a}$ commute with these coproducts, including their canonical inclusion and projection maps. This covers the empty family.

source.place: Tag 07D9, lemma-derived-products (1)-(2); good truncation formulas of def-kun-truncations

proof.text:
For either $T$, classical $A_T$-module sheaves are precisely the essential image of the exact fully faithful left adjoint $
u_T^*$ on étale module sheaves. If $M_s\simeq
u_T^*N_s$, the left-adjoint colimit theorem identifies $ igoplus_sM_s$ with $
u_T^*( igoplus_sN_s)$, hence it is classical. Therefore step 2 implies that ambient coproducts of classical-cohomology complexes again have classical cohomology. Their good truncations have classical cohomology as well, since each cohomology sheaf is either one of the original ones or zero. Moreover the exact termwise functor $
u_T^*$ preserves coproducts on the unbounded derived categories, by the exact-derived-coproduct theorem. No claim about essential surjectivity on unbounded complexes is used.

source.place: Transfer: compatibility with sums, used only on the bounded-below classical comparison

proof.text: Write $G=Rf_{\mathrm{proét},*}$. The ordinary constant-coefficient pro-étale operations give the unbounded adjunction $f^*\dashv G$; its left adjoint is exact and acts termwise. Thus $G$ preserves countable products by the right-adjoint limit theorem, and is triangulated and commutes with shifts by the K-injective right-derived-functor theorem. It preserves lower bounds: if $L\in D^{\ge a}(\mathcal A_X)$, choose a K-injective complex $J$ of injectives, zero in degrees below $a$, representing $L$. Then $f_*J$, which computes this same total $G(L)$, is zero below $a$. Consequently $G(L)\in D^{\ge a}(\mathcal A_Y)$.

source.place: Second paragraph: unbounded K-injective right adjoints preserve products; lower bounds via bounded-below injective representatives

proof.text: Set $c=2e$. There is an integer $n>0$ with $n1_A=0$: two of the finitely many elements $0,1_A,2\cdot1_A,\ldots$ coincide. Hence every $A$-module sheaf has torsion underlying abelian sheaf. The assumed fibre bound applies to $f$ itself, so the proper torsion cohomological-dimension theorem gives $R^qf_{\mathrm{ét},*}F=0$ for $q>c$ on underlying abelian sheaves. The higher-direct-image forgetful comparison and the faithful exact forgetful functor give the same vanishing for every étale $A$-module sheaf. Apply the finite-cd qcqs direct-image coproduct theorem with this fixed $c$: $E=Rf_{\mathrm{ét},*}$ preserves all small coproducts of arbitrary unbounded étale $A$-complexes, with the canonical maps induced by coprojections.

source.place: Tag 095U, lemma-cohomological-dimension-proper; Tag 0F0D, lemma-proper-mod-n-direct-sums, and finite-cd coproduct theorem; coefficient comparison is Tag 0D6J, sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-modules-abelian-unbounded

proof.text:
Let $M$ be any classical $A_X$-module sheaf and write $M\simeq
u_X^*F$ using the module-sheaf comparison equivalence. Apply the canonical bounded-below direct-image comparison to $F[0]$: $G(M[0])\simeq
u_Y^*Rf_{\mathrm{ét},*}(F[0])$. Compatibility of bounded-below and total right derived functors identifies its cohomology with the classical higher direct images. By step 5 these vanish for $q>c$. Exactness of $
u_Y^*$, with its natural cohomology identification, proves $H^q(G(M[0]))=0$ for $q>c$. All these comparisons concern bounded-below inputs, not arbitrary unbounded étale origins.

source.place: Transfer: bounded-below direct-image comparison applied to a classical sheaf

proof.text: Countable products in both pro-étale module categories are exact, and the canonical truncation tower is left complete. Their derived countable products exist and are represented by termwise products. Apply the class-relative left-complete heart upper-bound theorem with source $\mathcal A_X$, target $\mathcal A_Y$, functor $G$, class $\mathcal S$ of classical module sheaves, and bound $c$. Its functor hypotheses are step 4 and its heart hypothesis is step 6. It follows that, for every classical-cohomology $L$ and integer $b$, $L\in D^{\le b}$ implies $G(L)\in D^{\le b+c}$. This controls the entire unbounded negative tail; it imposes no cohomological bound on nonclassical heart objects or on a ground field.

source.place: Tag 07KC, lemma-products; Tag 08TC, definition-derived-limit; Tag 0H72, remark-map-into-derived-limit-truncations; class-relative bound as stated by lem-sfb-left-complete-heart-upper-bound

proof.text:
First consider a family $(L_s)$ with classical cohomology in one common interval $[a,b]$. The bounded-below derived unit theorem and classical derived equivalence give étale complexes $B_s$ and isomorphisms $
u_X^*B_s\simeq L_s$. Exact faithful $
u_X^*$ reflects vanishing of cohomology, so each $B_s$ lies in $[a,b]$; their étale coproduct also lies there by step 2. The bounded-below direct-image comparison applies both to every $B_s$ and to $ igoplus_sB_s$. Combining it with step 3 (derived $
u_X^*,
u_Y^*$ preserve sums) and step 5 ($E$ preserves sums) gives isomorphisms
$$ igoplus_sG L_s\simeq
u_Y^* igoplus_s E B_s\xrightarrow{\sim}
u_Y^*E( igoplus_sB_s)\xrightarrow{\sim}G(
u_X^* igoplus_sB_s)\simeq G( igoplus_sL_s).$$
This composite is the canonical comparison: on the $s$-th coprojection it is $G$ of the corresponding coprojection, by naturality of the direct-image comparison and of the chosen isomorphisms. Thus the actual comparison is invertible on uniformly bounded families. No unbounded étale/pro-étale equivalence has been assumed.

source.place: Étale statements and Transfer: direct sums for the bounded truncation windows

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary integer $m$. For the given family define $U_s=\tau_{\le m}K_s$, with inclusion $u_s:U_s\to K_s$. The standard truncation triangle has third term $\tau_{\ge m+1}K_s$. By step 4 its image under $G$ lies in degrees at least $m+1$. Apply $G$ to the triangle and read the long exact sequence in degrees $m-1,m$: the two groups of the third term vanish, hence $H^m(G u_s)$ is an isomorphism. All $U_s$ retain classical cohomology by step 3.

source.place: Étale statements: finite cohomological window, first remove the upper tail

proof.text: Put $V_s=\tau_{\ge m-c}U_s$, with projection $v_s:U_s\to V_s$. These complexes have classical cohomology and lie in the common finite interval $[m-c,m]$. The first term of the truncation triangle for $v_s$ is $W_s=\tau_{\le m-c-1}U_s$. It has classical cohomology and is at most $m-c-1$, so step 7 gives $G W_s\in D^{\le m-1}$. In particular $H^m(GW_s)=H^{m+1}(GW_s)=0$. The long exact sequence after applying $G$ therefore makes $H^m(Gv_s)$ an isomorphism. Step 8 applies to the family $(V_s)$.

source.place: Étale statements: finite cohomological window, remove the lower tail using the uniform bound

proof.text: The same two computations apply to the ambient sum $K=\bigoplus_sK_s$: by steps 2–3 it has classical cohomology and its truncations identify, with the canonical arrows, with $U=\bigoplus_sU_s$ and $V=\bigoplus_sV_s$. Hence $H^m(G(\bigoplus_su_s))$ and $H^m(G(\bigoplus_sv_s))$ are isomorphisms by steps 9–10. On the other side, the canonical cohomology/coproduct identification of step 2 shows that $H^m(\bigoplus_sG u_s)$ and $H^m(\bigoplus_sG v_s)$ are the coproducts of the isomorphisms proved in those steps, hence are isomorphisms. The bounds here depend only on $m,c$, and not on $s$.

source.place: Étale statements: apply the uniform finite window to each summand and to their ambient sum

proof.text:
For a family $T_s$ write $\sigma_T:\bigoplus_sGT_s\to G(\bigoplus_sT_s)$ for the comparison. Its naturality for a family of arrows $h_s:T_s\to T'_s$ is the equality
$$G(\bigoplus_sh_s)\,\sigma_T=\sigma_{T'}\,(\bigoplus_sGh_s).$$
Indeed both sides composed with the $s$-th coprojection equal $G(\iota'_sh_s)$; the coproduct universal property gives equality. Apply this to $u_s$ and $v_s$. After $H^m$, all vertical maps in the two resulting squares are isomorphisms by step 11, and $H^m(\sigma_V)$ is an isomorphism by step 8. Cancellation first gives invertibility of $H^m(\sigma_U)$, then of $H^m(\sigma_K)$. Since $m$ was arbitrary, the unbounded derived cohomology criterion makes $\sigma_K$ an isomorphism. For $I=\varnothing$ all sums are zero, and additive $G$ sends zero to zero; the same comparison is the unique isomorphism $0\to0$.
